previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with a flare of chronic pancreatitis, presenting with epigastric pain radiating to the back, nausea, vomiting, and inability to tolerate oral intake. She also reported dysuria and was found to have a urinary tract infection caused by E. coli, which was treated with ciprofloxacin. Her pain was managed with IV fluids and a transition from IV to oral analgesics, including tramadol, while avoiding narcotics. Blood pressure was elevated during stress and pain episodes, leading to an increase in lisinopril from 10 mg to 30 mg daily. She remained on levetiracetam for seizure prevention, with plans to transition to lamictal. The patient improved over the course of admission, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with services after demonstrating stability on her outpatient medication regimen. Follow-up was arranged with her PCP, neurology, and a partial psychiatric program she had previously missed due to hospitalization.

radiology_notes.text:
PICC LINE PLACEMENT

INDICATION:  IV access needed for hydration.

The procedure was explained to the patient.  A timeout was performed.

RADIOLOGIST:  Dr. ___ performed the procedure.

TECHNIQUE:  Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the right brachial
vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a micropuncture set.
Hard copies of ultrasound images were obtained before and immediately after
establishing intravenous access.  A peel-away sheath was then placed over a
guidewire and a double-lumen power PICC line measuring 34 cm in length was
then placed through the peel-away sheath with its tip positioned in the SVC
under fluoroscopic guidance.  Position of the catheter was confirmed by a
fluoroscopic spot film of the chest.

The peel-away sheath and guidewire were then removed.  The catheter was
secured to the skin, flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well.  There were no immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION:  Uncomplicated ultrasound and fluoroscopically guided double-lumen
power PICC line placement via the right brachial venous approach.  Final
internal length is 34 cm, with the tip positioned in SVC.  The line is ready
to use.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with chronic pancreatitis with increasing
vomiting and hematocrit drop.  Evaluate for pancreatic pseudocyst.

COMPARISON:  Liver and gallbladder ultrasound, ___.

ABDOMINAL ULTRASOUND:  The liver appears normal in echotexture with no focal
liver lesions identified.  There is no intrahepatic billiary duct dilation.
The common bile duct measures 0.7 cm.  The patient is status post
cholecystectomy.  The spleen measures 12.5 cm.  The visualized head and body
of the pancreas shows no abnormality.  The tail of the pancreas was not well
visualized and was obscured by overlying bowel gas. There are no focal fluid
collections in the vicinity of the pancreas. The main portal vein is patent. 
Limited evaluation of the kidneys show no evidence of hydronephrosis or renal
calculi.

IMPRESSION:
Pancreatic tail was not well visualized, however, no focal fluid collections
in the vicinity of the pancreas to suggest pancreatic pseudocyst.

HISTORY:  ___ year old woman with chronic pancreatitis, needs PICC for
hydration and current PICC is leaking at skin insertion site. 

COMPARISON:  PICC placement from ___. 

FINDINGS:  PICC LINE EXCHANGE / REPOSITIONING
                            
The procedure was explained to the patient. A timeout was performed. 

RADIOLOGIST: Dr. ___ (resident) and Dr. ___ (attending)
performed the procedure.

TECHNIQUE: Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, a guidewire was
advanced through the indwelling right arm PICC line, and subsequently into the
SVC under fluoroscopic guidance. The old PICC line was then removed and a
peel-away sheath was then placed over the guidewire. A new double lumen power
PICC line measuring 34 cm in length was then placed through the peel-away
sheath with its tip positioned in the SVC under fluoroscopic guidance.
Position of the catheter was confirmed by a fluoroscopic spot film of the
chest.
The peel-away sheath and guidewire were then removed. The catheter was secured
to the skin, flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.
The patient tolerated the procedure well. There were no immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION: Uncomplicated fluoroscopically guided PICC line exchange for a new
double lumen power PICC line. Final internal length is 34 cm, with the tip
positioned in the SVC. The line is ready to use.
